Farther from the point of attachment to the trunk. The foot is distal to the tibia.

Farther from the body surface. The heart is deep to the ribs.
On the same side of the body. The radius and ulna of one arm are ipsilateral.
On opposite sides of the body. The two hands are contralateral to each other.

questions.prompt: Define anatomical position and write one sentence describing a structure's location using at least two directional terms.
questions.modelAnswer: Standing upright, feet flat, arms at the sides, palms and face forward. Example: the sternum is anterior and medial to the ribs.

questions.prompt: Is the median plane a sagittal, frontal, or transverse plane? What makes it 'median' specifically?
questions.modelAnswer: It is a sagittal plane. It is called median because it passes exactly through the midline, dividing the body into equal left and right halves; any other sagittal plane is parasagittal.

questions.prompt: Which plane divides the body into anterior and posterior portions? Which divides it into superior and inferior portions?
questions.modelAnswer: The frontal (coronal) plane divides anterior from posterior. The transverse (horizontal) plane divides superior from inferior.

questions.prompt: In strict anatomical terminology, what is the difference between 'arm' and 'leg' versus how these words are used in everyday conversation?
questions.modelAnswer: Anatomically the arm (brachium) is only shoulder to elbow, and the leg (crus) is only knee to ankle. Everyday speech uses arm for the whole upper limb and leg for the whole lower limb. The forearm is antebrachial and the thigh is femoral.

questions.prompt: Why do anatomists always describe the body as if it were in anatomical position, even when a patient is lying down or in an unusual posture?
questions.modelAnswer: So that every directional term has one fixed meaning regardless of how the body is actually positioned. Everyone pictures the same reference frame, which prevents ambiguity.

questions.prompt: Write a true sentence using proximal/distal and two structures.
questions.modelAnswer: The elbow is proximal to the wrist; the wrist is distal to the elbow.

questions.prompt: Explain why a single misspelled or mispronounced anatomical term could matter in a clinical setting. Give an example.
questions.modelAnswer: Many terms differ by one letter and name completely different structures: ilium (hip bone) vs ileum (small intestine), malleus (ear) vs malleolus (ankle), gustation (taste) vs gestation (pregnancy). A one-letter slip can send a clinician to the wrong organ system.
